hints.title: Two-Pass Traversal Elimination Obstacle
hints.text: Finding the kth node from the end by measuring total length requires two passes. How can keeping a fixed window between two reference markers locate the kth from end concurrently?

hints.title: Fixed Gap Distance Invariant
hints.text: Locate the kth node from start as first. Then slide a second pointer starting from head alongside a probe starting from first until probe reaches tail.

hints.title: Fixed-Offset Value Swap Procedure
hints.text: Advance first k - 1 steps from head. Set second to head and curr to first. While curr.next exists, advance both curr and second. Swap the values of first and second. Return head.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def swapNodes(self, head: Optional[ListNode], k: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        first = head
        for _ in range(k - 1):
            first = first.next
        second = head
        curr = first
        while curr.next:
            curr = curr.next
            second = second.next
        first.val, second.val = second.val, first.val
        return head
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single pass locating both kth nodes and swapping their values.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Counting total length first requires two traversals instead of a single pass.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Fixed-window traversal finds the symmetric node in O(1) space in one pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that exchanging node values solves this problem cleanly without complex link rewiring.
